newsitem.title: BRUNEI: Brunei offers new incentives to beckon investors.
newsitem.headline: Brunei offers new incentives to beckon investors.

text.p: Brunei's Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah on Tuesday announced that he will offer new incentives to investors as the country continues its push away from dependence upon oil.

In a speech marking his 51st birthday, the sultan said financial loan guarantees, industrial development schemes as well as loan facilities for regional business investment and for project studies would be offered.
Brunei was also considering plans to improve other incentives such as equity, tax, land ownership and incentives for export and high-technology industry, he said.
"We will have to flow with the current. But we will have to do this wisely and with caution," he said.
"Black gold" is slowly running out in the tiny sultanate on Borneo island, and the government has been trying to boost the industrial sector and tourism.
Hassanal, considered the world's richest man with a reported net worth of $38 billion, said Brunei would soon come up with a master plan for the tourism industry.
It plans to be a service hub for trade and tourism by 2003.

Celebrations for the Sultan's 51st birthday were much scaled down compared to his 50th last year, when pop superstar Michael Jackson performed free of charge, and Britain's Prince Charles flew in to play polo with Hassanal.
